summary.intent: Ship phase 62 (unified node codec core keystone) through all quality gates: security audit, Nyquist validation, D-02 gate, simplify review, and CodeRabbit, then commit the phase documentation.
summary.outcome: All gates passed — 190 core codec tests green, builds clean, security 12/12 closed, Nyquist 11/11 compliant. Phase docs and three deferred todos committed unsigned (session-wide state).

repo: All phase-62 commits are unsigned (commit.gpgsign: false in this environment) — this is session-wide, not a one-off; flag for merge decision if PR enforces signatures.

scripts tsc 'command not found' is a local PATH issue in bash -lc invocations, not a real failure; phase 62 didn't touch tsconfig.scripts.json.

code.finding: Correctly composes Phase-61 primitive with correct role bytes, no reimplementation, terminal-owner zeroization respected — clean simplify result.

workflow: The 2-minute 'signing hang' was actually the slow pre-commit hook (lint-staged + check-api-client.sh), not a 1Password signer wedge — the commit landed fine.
Parallelizing security auditor, CodeRabbit CLI, and D-02 gate as background jobs while doing the simplify review inline is an effective pattern for phase gates.
Scoping eslint to only phase-N paths (not the whole repo) is the reliable way to confirm gate-relevant lint cleanliness without noise from unrelated generated files.
Committing .planning/ docs separately from code is fast because .md files skip the slow eslint pre-commit step.

friction: git commit appeared to hang (timed out at 2m) due to slow pre-commit hooks (lint-staged + check-api-client.sh), causing false alarm about 1Password signer wedge.
